title: Introduce RAG tool-fallback patterns and lightweight browser playground
author: Marcel Nguyen
description: Motivation: Provide concrete, production-oriented examples for handling downstream tool failures in RAG/agent flows and offer a tiny browser-based playground that lets engineers iterate on fallback policies locally. This PR adds three companion artifacts: 1) a set of RAG template patterns demonstrating progressive fallback (primary vector store -> reduced-context search -> cached snippet -> hallucination-safe default) with policy hooks and telemetry probes, 2) a minimal agent/tool-calling examples folder that includes retry/backoff, circuit-breaker, and graceful degrade utilities for tool adapters, and 3) a lightweight browser playground (DevContainer + static UI) to exercise different fallback strategies without a full backend. What changed: added new examples under redwood-examples/rag/fallback-patterns, included TypeScript agent stubs and adapter wrappers under redwood-examples/agents/tool-adapters, updated quickstart README with step-by-step setup and recommended telemetry probes, and patched the docs site navigation to surface these examples (docs link points to /examples/rag/fallback-patterns). This is intended as a low-friction learning path for platform and application engineers to test trade-offs between latency, cost, and answer-quality when external tools or indexes fail. Testing and validation: local smoke scripts, CI lint/typecheck, and an e2e run in the browser playground that simulates index failures and verifies policy outcomes. Known limitations: the browser playground uses an in-memory stub for secrets and should not be used for sensitive data; production deployment requires the adapter KMS/HSM integration (covered in a follow-up). Related: ENG-3421 (fallback telemetry) and PM-1176 (quickstart adoption metrics).
commits: 1) Add fallback pattern templates and policy examples; 2) Implement tool-adapter wrappers (retry, circuit-breaker, degrade); 3) Add browser playground DevContainer and static UI; 4) Update README and docs site links; 5) Small test and CI fixes to type imports
review_comments: Lina Torres (review): Nice pattern set. Please add explicit examples showing metric names and suggested cardinality for the telemetry probes so SRE can onboard faster.
Marcel Nguyen (reply): Good call — added a telemetry.md snippet with metric names and labels in the latest patch, and added a recommended retention note.
Ethan Brooks (review): The circuit-breaker default thresholds look aggressive for high-cardinality workloads. Can we expose config and a short benchmarking script to choose thresholds?
Marcel Nguyen (reply): Exposed thresholds via config and added a small bench script (bench/circuit-thresholds.sh) that runs locally against the playground stub; documented guidance in README.

Priya Menon (review): Docs nav change is fine but please ensure the new examples are discoverable from the RAG quickstarts page. Also add a short video GIF showing the playground run for the docs site.
Marcel Nguyen (reply): Added a small animated GIF (docs/assets/playground-run.gif) and wired a link from docs/rag/quickstarts to the new examples folder.
